ios.desc:
Do you ever unlock your phone to check an email, and suddenly realize you've been scrolling for 45 minutes? You didn't make a conscious decision to open the app. Your thumbs just did it — complete autopilot.

Welcome to PIM — Please Inconvenience Me.

PIM is not a strict app-blocker or a screen time monitor. Instead, it fights phone addiction and improves your digital wellbeing by adding some friction to your worst screen habits.

It's not that you lack willpower. Your phone is just too easy to use. Social media apps are designed for zero effort. Just one tap, and the addictive content hits your brain like a drug.

PIM gives your willpower a fighting chance. Try PIM free for 7 days with unlimited apps and full features. If it works for you, a one-time purchase keeps it forever. 

When you try to open a restricted app, PIM stops you. To actually use the app, you have to complete a short cognitive speedbump — like a typing task, a math problem, or a screen-tapping exercise.

Yes, it's inconvenient. But the inconvenience is the point — not everything should be convenient. It gives your brain the time it needs to reset and snap out of autopilot.

--------------------

NO SUBSCRIPTIONS, NO SURPRISES
Try PIM free for 7 days -- unlimited apps, full features. No ads, no up-front credit card. 
One-time purchase to keep it forever.

DESIGN YOUR OWN FRICTION
Customize the task to the temptation. Put tough arithmetic on your worst doomscrolling apps, a simple tapping task for email. Choose easy, medium, hard, or fully custom.

LIMIT ACCESS
Once you finish the task, your app unlocks for 1 to 60 minutes. When time's up, time's up - or do another task.

LOCK YOUR SETTINGS
Password-lock your settings so you can't bypass your own rules in a moment of temptation.

quotes.text:
A while back I opened YouTube to grab a recipe, planning to start dinner right after. 45 minutes later I "woke up" from the Shorts trance. No dinner started, and I never even got the recipe.

That kind of thing kept happening, and it's not a willpower problem. Web pages used to have a "more" button at the bottom. That one tap was a decision point, and it got "designed away" around 2006. Infinite scroll exists precisely because even that much friction reduced usage. Thousands of very smart people have spent twenty years removing every barrier between you and the endless feed.

I tried a bunch of focus/screen time apps, and just didn't like them. They were complex, with all kinds of different modes. And everything was all about getting you to subscribe - but I avoid subscriptions like the plague.

PIM (Please Inconvenience Me) is me putting the friction back. It doesn't block apps, but when you open a restricted one, you need to complete a task. Like some typing, basic arithmetic, or tapping dots on the screen (what I like to call "the world's most boring video game").

You're never locked out. You just can't get in - or continue beyond your session time - without some effort. And you can customize the difficulty, make it as easy or hard as you like.

It's on both Android and iPhone:
Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.pleaseinconvenienceme.pim
iPhone: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/pim-please-inconvenience-me/id6761953470
